Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 60, verse 1 (part 1 of 2):

The Surah al-Mumtahanah is Madani by the consensus of scholars, and it has thirteen verses. Al-Mumtahanah (with a kasra on the ha') means "the one who tests," that is, the one who tests. The act is ascribed to the surah metaphorically, just as the surah "Bara'ah" is called al-Muba'thirah (the one that uncovers) and al-Fadihah (the one that exposes), because it uncovered the defects of the hypocrites. Whoever says al-Mumtahanah (with a fatha on the ha') ascribes the surah to the woman about whom it was revealed, who was Umm Kulthum, daughter of Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt. God Most High said: ﴿So test them; God knows best their faith﴾ [60:10], the verse [[See p. 61 of this part.]]. She was the wife of Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, and she bore him Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Rahman.

In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.
In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

O you who have believed, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies, extending to them affection, while they have disbelieved in what has come to you of the truth, expelling the Messenger and you [because] you believe in God, your Lord. If you have gone out striving in My way and seeking My good pleasure, [do you] confide to them with affection? I know best what you conceal and what you declare. And whoever of you does that has certainly strayed from the right way (1).

God Most High's words: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take My enemy and your enemy﴾ The verb "ittakhadha" (to take) takes two objects, and they are "your enemy" and "allies" (awliya'). The word "'aduw" (enemy) is on the pattern fa'ul, from "'adā," like "'afuww" from "'afā." Because it is on the pattern of the verbal noun, it applies to the group just as it applies to the individual. In this verse there are seven issues.

The first issue: God Most High's words: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take My enemy and your enemy﴾. The imams narrated, and the wording is Muslim's, from Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ sent me, al-Zubayr and al-Miqdad, and said: "Go to Rawdat Khakh [[A place between Makkah and Madinah, twelve miles from Madinah.]], for there is a woman in a howdah [[The zaʿina is the woman in a howdah. The word zaʿina is not used except for that.]] with a letter; take it from her." So we set off, our horses galloping [[That is, running.]] with us, and suddenly we came upon the woman. We said: "Bring out the letter." She said: "I have no letter." We said: "You will bring out the letter, or we will strip you of your clothes." So she brought it out from her braid. We brought it to the Messenger of God ﷺ, and in it was: "From Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah ... to some of the polytheists of Makkah, informing them of some of the affairs of the Messenger of God ﷺ." The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "O Hatib, what is this?" He said: "Do not hasten against me, O Messenger of God. I was a man attached to Quraysh" (Sufyan said: he was their ally, and not one of their own people), "and among those who were with you of the Emigrants, there are those who have relatives who protect their families. So I wanted, since I lacked kinship with them, to make a hand among them by which they would protect my relatives. I did not do it out of disbelief, nor apostasy from my religion, nor out of contentment with disbelief after Islam." The Prophet ﷺ said: "He has spoken the truth." Umar said: "Let me, O Messenger of God, strike the neck of this hypocrite." He said: "He has witnessed Badr, and what would make you know? Perhaps God looked upon the people of Badr and said, 'Do what you wish, for I have forgiven you.'" Then God the Mighty and Majestic revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies﴾. It was said: the woman's name was Sarah, a client of the Quraysh. The letter read: "To proceed: the Messenger of God ﷺ has turned toward you with an army like the night, moving like a torrent. I swear by God, even if he went toward you alone, God would give him victory over you and fulfil His promise to him concerning you, for God is his protector and his helper." Some exegetes mentioned this.

Al-Qushayri and al-Tha'labi mentioned that Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah was a man from Yemen, and he had an alliance in Makkah with the Banu Asad ibn Abd al-Uzza, the clan of al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam. It was also said that he was an ally of al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam. Sarah, the client of Abu Amr ibn Sayfi ibn Hisham ibn Abd Manaf, came from Makkah to Madinah while the Messenger of God ﷺ was preparing for the conquest of Makkah. It was also said that this happened at the time of al-Hudaybiyah. The Messenger of God ﷺ said to her: "Have you come as an emigrant, O Sarah?" She said: "No." He said: "Have you come as a Muslim?" She said: "No." He said: "Then what brought you?" She said: "You are the family, the clients, the origin and the tribe, and the clients have gone" (meaning they were killed on the day of Badr), "and I have been in great need, so I came to you so that you would give me and clothe me." The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Then where are you from the youths of the people of Makkah?" She was a singer. She said: "No one has asked anything of me since the battle of Badr." So the Messenger of God ﷺ urged the Banu Abd al-Muttalib and the Banu al-Muttalib to give to her, and they clothed her and gave to her and provided her with a mount, and she went out toward Makkah. Hatib came to her and said: "I will give you ten dinars and a cloak, on condition that you deliver this letter to the people of Makkah." He wrote in the letter: "The Messenger of God ﷺ intends you, so take your precautions." Sarah set out, and Gabriel descended and informed the Prophet ﷺ of that. So he sent Ali, al-Zubayr and Abu Martha al-Ghanawi. In another narration: Ali, al-Zubayr and al-Miqdad. In another narration: he sent Ali and Ammar ibn Yasir. In another narration: Ali, Ammar, Umar, al-Zubayr, Talhah, al-Miqdad and Abu Martha, and they were all horsemen. He said to them: "Set out until you reach Rawdat Khakh, for there is a woman in a howdah, and with her is a letter from Hatib to the polytheists. Take it from her and let her go her way. If she does not hand it over to you, then strike her neck." They overtook her at that place, and they said to her: "Where is the letter?" She swore that she had no letter. They searched her belongings and did not find a letter with her. They were about to return, when Ali said: "By God, we have not lied, nor have we been lied to!" He drew his sword and said: "Bring out the letter, or by God I will strip you and strike your neck." When she saw his earnestness, she brought it out from her hair-knot [[In another narration, from her waistband. The hujzah is the knot of the izar, and the place of the tie of the trousers.]]. They let her go her way and returned with the letter to the Messenger of God ﷺ. He sent for Hatib and said: "Do you recognize this letter?" He said: "Yes." And he mentioned the hadith [[Hadith: a report of the words or deeds of the Prophet ﷺ.]] in substance as preceded. It is narrated that the Prophet ﷺ granted safety to all the people on the day of the Conquest except four, and Hatib was not one of them.

The second issue: The surah is a foundation for the prohibition of allying with the disbelievers, and this has been discussed in more than one place [[See vol. 4 pp. 57 and 178, and vol. 6 p. 216.]]. Among this is God Most High's words: ﴿Let not the believers take the disbelievers as allies rather than the believers﴾ [Ali Imran: 28]. ﴿O you who have believed, do not take for intimate friends those other than yourselves﴾ [Ali Imran: 118]. ﴿O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 51]. There are many like these. It is mentioned that when Hatib heard "O you who have believed," he fainted from joy at being addressed with the word of faith.

The third issue: God Most High's words: ﴿you extend to them affection﴾. This means outwardly, because Hatib's heart was sound, as evidenced by the Prophet ﷺ saying to them: "As for your companion, he has spoken the truth." This is explicit proof of the soundness of his heart and the purity of his belief. The "ba'" in "bil-mawaddah" (with affection) is superfluous, as you say: "I read the surah" and "I read with the surah," and "I threw to him what was in my soul" and "with what was in my soul." It is also permissible that it be retained, with the object of "tulqun" (you extend) being omitted, meaning: you extend to them the news of the Messenger of God ﷺ because of the affection that is between you and them. Likewise ﴿you confide to them with affection﴾, that is, because of affection. Al-Farra' said: "tulqun ilayhim bil-mawaddah" is connected to "awliya'," and the entering and leaving of the "ba'" with "mawaddah" is the same. It is also permissible that it be connected to ﴿do not take﴾ as a circumstantial clause (hal) from its subject pronoun, and with ﴿allies﴾ as its qualifier, and it is permissible that it be a new sentence. The meaning of ﴿you extend to them affection﴾ is: you inform them of the secrets of the Muslims and give them counsel. Al-Zajjaj said this.

The fourth issue: Whoever frequently spies on the weaknesses of the Muslims, alerts [the enemy] to them, and informs their enemy of their news, is not thereby a disbeliever, provided he does it for a worldly purpose and his belief remains sound, as Hatib did when he intended by that to make a hand [among them], and did not intend apostasy from the religion.

The fifth issue: If we say that by this he is not a disbeliever, is he then to be killed as a prescribed punishment (hadd) or not? The people differed on this. Malik, Ibn al-Qasim and Ashhab said: the Imam shall exercise his judgment in this. Abd al-Malik said: if that was his habit, he is to be killed, because he is a spy, and Malik has said that a spy is to be killed. This is sound, because of his harm to the Muslims and his striving for corruption on earth. Perhaps Ibn al-Majishun only took the repetition [of the act] as a condition in this because Hatib was apprehended at the beginning of his action. And God knows best.

The sixth issue: If the spy is a disbeliever, al-Awza'i said: it would constitute a breach of his covenant. Asbagh said: a spy from among the non-Muslim foreigners (harbi) is to be killed, while a Muslim spy and a dhimmi (non-Muslim under the protection of the Muslim state) are to be punished, unless they openly support the enemies of Islam, in which case both are to be killed. It has been narrated from Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet ﷺ was brought a spy of the polytheists named Furat ibn Hayyan, and he ordered him to be killed. He cried out: "O company of the Ansar, I am being killed, while I testify that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God!" So the Prophet ﷺ ordered him released. Then he said: "Among you are those I leave to their faith, and among them is Furat ibn Hayyan."

God's words ﴿while they have disbelieved﴾ are a circumstantial clause, either from "do not take" or from "you extend," meaning: do not befriend them or show them affection, when this is their condition. Al-Jahdari recited "limma ja'akum" (because of what has come to you), meaning: they disbelieved because of what has come to you of the truth.

The seventh issue: God Most High's words: ﴿expelling the Messenger﴾ are a resumed statement, as an explanation of their disbelief and their defiance, or a circumstantial clause from "they disbelieved." ﴿and you, [because] you believe in God, your Lord﴾ is a reason for "expelling," meaning: they expel the Messenger and expel you from Makkah because you believe in God, that is, because of your belief in God. Ibn Abbas said: Hatib was among those who were expelled with the Prophet ﷺ. It was also said: there is inversion in the speech, and the meaning is: do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies if you have gone out striving in My way. It was also said: there is an omission in the speech, and the meaning is: if you have gone out striving in My way and seeking My good pleasure, then do not extend affection to them. It was also said: ﴿if you have gone out striving in My way and seeking My good pleasure﴾ is a condition whose answer is placed first, and the meaning is: if you have gone out striving in My way, then do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies. "Jihadan" (striving) and "ibtighaa'" (seeking) are in the accusative because they are objects of purpose (maf'ul lahu). God's words ﴿you confide to them with affection﴾ are a substitute for ﴿you extend﴾ and an explanation of it. Verbs may substitute for verbs, as God Most High said: ﴿And whoever does that will meet a penalty. The punishment will be doubled for him﴾ [al-Furqan: 68–69]. Sibawayh quoted:

"Whenever you come to us, you will visit us in our homes,
you will find firewood well cut and a fire blazing."

It was also said: it is on the assumption that "you confide to them with affection," in which case it is a new sentence. All of this is a rebuke to Hatib, and it indicates his excellence, his nobility, his sincere counsel to the Messenger of God ﷺ, and the truthfulness of his faith, for rebuke only comes from one who loves his beloved. As someone said:

"I rebuke a friend who holds affection for me
when estrangement from him troubles me.
If rebuke departs, there is no affection left,
and affection remains as long as rebuke remains."

Its meaning, "with affection," is "with counsel" in the letter sent to them. The bā' (in bil-mawaddah) is superfluous (ziyādah), as we have mentioned, or it is established and not superfluous.

His, the Exalted's, statement: ﴿And I know best what you conceal﴾ (aḍmartum, what you hid in your hearts) "and what you disclose" (aẓhartum, what you made apparent). The bā' in bimā is superfluous; it is said: "I knew such-and-such" and "I knew of such-and-such" (ʿalimtu kadhā wa-ʿalimtu bikadhā). It was also said: "And I know, of everyone, what you conceal and what you disclose," so "of everyone" has been omitted, as one says "So-and-so is more knowing and more excellent than others." Ibn ʿAbbas said: "And I know best what you conceal in your breasts, and what you make apparent with your tongues of acknowledgment and affirmation of God's oneness."

(And whoever among you does it) i.e., whoever among you secretly conveys information to them and corresponds with them (then he has strayed from the right way) i.e., he has missed the direct path.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 60, verse 2:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿If they overcome you﴾, meaning they encounter you and come upon you. From this comes al-muthaqafah (sparring, a contest of skill), that is, seeking to catch the opponent off guard in swordplay and the like. It was also said: "If they overcome you" means they gain the upper hand over you and gain power over you. ﴿They will be your enemies and will stretch out their hands and their tongues against you with evil﴾, meaning their hands with striking and killing, and their tongues with insult.

﴿And they wish that you would disbelieve﴾ in Muhammad (ﷺ). So do not give them counsel, for they do not give you counsel.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 60, verse 3:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Your relatives and your children will not benefit you on the Day of Resurrection. He will separate you﴾. When Hatib made his excuse that he had children and relatives among them, the Lord, mighty and majestic, made clear that family and children will benefit no one on the Day of Resurrection if disobedience was committed for their sake.

(Yafsilu baynakum) meaning He will admit the believers to Paradise and admit the disbelievers to the Fire. There are seven readings of "yafsilu". ʿĀṣim read "yafsilu" with a fatha on the yāʾ and a kasra on the ṣād, lightened (mukhaffafan). Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read it doubled (mushaddadan), except that it is in the passive form (ʿalā mā lam yusamma fāʿiluhu). Ṭalḥah and al-Nakhaʿī read it with a nūn and a doubled kasra on the ṣād. It is also narrated from ʿAlqamah in the same way with a nūn and a lightened ṣād. Qatādah and Abū Ḥaywah read "yufṣilu" with a ḍamma on the yāʾ and a kasra on the ṣād, lightened, from afṣala. The rest read "yufṣalu" with a ḍammed yāʾ, a lightened fāʾ and a fatha on the ṣād, in the passive form; Abū ʿUbayd preferred this reading. As for the one who lightened it, his basis is His saying: ﴿And He is the best of judges﴾ [al-Anʿam: 57], and His saying: ﴿Indeed, the Day of Judgement (yawm al-faṣl) is the appointed time for them all﴾ [al-Dukhān: 40]. As for the one who doubled it, the reason is that this form is clearer for a verb that is frequent, repeated and recurring. As for the one who recited it in the passive form, the reason is that the agent is known. As for the one who recited it in the active form, he returned the pronoun to Allah, exalted is He. As for the one who read with a nūn, it is out of magnification (al-taʿẓīm).

(And Allah is Seeing of what you do.)

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 60, verse 4–5:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿There has already been for you an excellent example in Ibrahim﴾. When Allah, mighty and majestic, forbade taking disbelievers as allies (muwalah), He mentioned the story of Ibrahim, peace be upon him, and that part of his conduct was disavowing the disbelievers. That is, follow him and take him as your model, except in his asking forgiveness for his father. Al-iswah and al-uswah are what one takes as a model (yutaʾassa bihi), like al-qidwah and al-qudwah. It is said: he is your iswah, meaning he is like you and you are like him. ʿAsim recited uswah with a dammah on the hamzah; both are dialects.

(And those who were with him) meaning Ibrahim's companions among the believers. Ibn Zayd said: they are the prophets. (When they said to their people) the disbelievers: ﴿Indeed, we are free of you and of what you worship besides Allah﴾, meaning the idols. Buraʾu is the plural of barīʾ, like sharīk and shurakaʾ, and ẓarīf and ẓurafaʾ. The common reading follows the pattern fuʿalaʾ. ʿIsa ibn ʿUmar and Ibn Abi Ishaq read "biraʾ" with a kasrah on the bāʾ, on the pattern fiʿal, like qaṣīr and qiṣar, ṭawīl and ṭiwal, ẓarīf and ẓirāf. It is permissible to drop the hamzah, so that you say: bara, and with tanwin. It is also read "biraʾun" as a description by the verbal noun. It is read "burāʾ" by changing the kasrah to a dammah, like rukhāl and rubāb [Rukhal: plural of rakhl, the female young of sheep. Rubab: plural of rabaʾ, a ewe that has recently given birth; it is said also: one whose young has died].

The verse is an explicit command to follow Ibrahim, peace be upon him, in his action, and this confirms that the law of those before us is law for us in what Allah and His Messenger report.

(We reject you) meaning we reject what you believe in of idols. It is also said: meaning your deeds; we deny them and reject that you are upon the truth.

(And there has appeared between us and you enmity and hatred forever) meaning this is our way with you as long as you remain in your disbelief, (until you believe in Allah alone). Then enmity turns into allegiance. (Except the saying of Ibrahim to his father: ﴿I will surely ask forgiveness for you﴾), so do not follow him in seeking forgiveness, lest you ask forgiveness for polytheists. He said it out of a promise he had made to him, as Qatadah, Mujahid and others said. It is also said: the meaning of the exception is that Ibrahim abandoned his people and distanced himself from them, except in asking forgiveness for his father; then he explained his excuse in Surah al-Tawbah [see vol. 8, p. 274]. This indicates the superiority of our Prophet, peace be upon him, over all the other prophets, because when we were commanded to follow him we were commanded with an unrestricted command, in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it﴾ [al-Hashr: 7] [see p. 17 of this part], whereas when we were commanded to follow Ibrahim, peace be upon him, an exception was made for some of his actions. It is also said: it is a disconnected exception, meaning: but Ibrahim's saying to his father, ﴿I will surely ask forgiveness for you﴾, occurred only because he thought he had become a Muslim; when it became clear to him that he had not, he disavowed him. On this basis, asking forgiveness is permissible for one who is thought to have embraced Islam, but you have not found any such supposition, so why do you ally with them?

(And I cannot avail you anything against Allah) this is from the saying of Ibrahim, peace be upon him, to his father, meaning I cannot ward off from you any of Allah's punishment if you associate partners with Him.

(Our Lord, upon You we have relied) this is from the supplication of Ibrahim, peace be upon him, and his companions. It is also said: He taught the believers to say this, meaning: disavow the disbelievers, rely upon Allah, and say: ﴿Our Lord, upon You we have relied﴾, meaning we have depended (on You). (And to You we have turned) meaning we have returned, (and to You is the destination) to You is the return in the Hereafter. (Our Lord, do not make us a trial for the disbelievers) meaning do not let our enemy prevail over us, lest they think they are upon the truth and be tempted by that. It is also said: do not give them power over us, lest they tempt us and torment us.

(Our Lord, forgive us; indeed You are the Mighty, the Wise).

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 60, verse 6–7:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿There has certainly been for you in them⦄ — i.e., in Ibrahim and those with him among the prophets and the awliya' (friends of God).

(an excellent example) — i.e., in disavowing the disbelievers. It was also said that it is repeated for emphasis. And it was said that the second was revealed some time after the first, and how numerous are the repeated expressions in the Qur'an in this manner.

(And whoever turns away) — i.e., from Islam and from accepting these admonitions — (then indeed Allah is the Free of need) — i.e., He did not impose worship upon them out of need for them.

(the Praiseworthy) — in His essence and His attributes. When this was revealed, the Muslims became hostile to their relatives among the polytheists, so Allah knew the intensity of the Muslims' distress over that, and then it was revealed: (It may be that Allah will bring about affection between you and those among them whom you have shown enmity to) — and this is by the disbeliever embracing Islam. Some of them did embrace Islam after the conquest of Makkah and mixed with the Muslims, such as Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, al-Harith ibn Hisham, Suhayl ibn 'Amr, and Hakim ibn Hizam. It was also said: the affection was the Prophet's ﷺ marriage to Umm Habibah bint Abi Sufyan, so the temper of Abu Sufyan softened at that point, and his stubbornness in enmity relaxed. [[al-'Arikah: temperament. "Lanat 'arikatuhu" means his pride was broken. al-Shakimah: haughtiness. From the bridle: the iron bar that lies across the mouth.]]

Ibn 'Abbas said: The affection after the conquest was the Prophet's ﷺ marriage to Umm Habibah bint Abi Sufyan. **The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Allah does not forbid you from those who do not fight you over religion﴾.** On this verse there are three issues.

**The first issue:** This verse is a concession from Allah the Exalted regarding maintaining ties of kinship and kindness with those who are not hostile to the believers and do not fight them. Ibn Zayd said: "This was at the beginning of Islam, when there was a truce and the command to fight had been set aside. Then it was abrogated (*nusikha*)." Qatadah said: "It was abrogated by ﴿Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾ [at-Tawbah: 5]." (*Naskh*, abrogation, means that a ruling from an earlier revelation is cancelled by a later one.) [See vol. 8, p. 136.]

It was also said: "This ruling was tied to a cause, which was the truce. When the truce ended with the conquest of Makkah, the ruling was abrogated, but the wording remained recited." It was also said: "The verse is specific to the allies of the Prophet ﷺ and to those who had a covenant with him that they did not break." This was said by al-Hasan. Al-Kalbi said: "They are Khuza'ah and the Banu al-Harith ibn Abd Manaf." Abu Salih said the same and added: "They are Khuza'ah."

Mujahid said: "It is specific to those who believed but did not emigrate." It was also said: "It refers to women and children, because they are among those who do not fight, so Allah permitted kindness toward them." Some commentators reported this.

Most scholars of interpretation (*ahl al-ta'wil*) said: "The verse is *muhkam*" (*muhkam* means a ruling that has not been abrogated). They based this on the report that Asma' bint Abi Bakr asked the Prophet ﷺ: "Should I keep ties with my mother when she comes to me as a polytheist?" He said: "Yes." This was recorded by al-Bukhari and Muslim.

It was also said that the verse was revealed about this matter. Amir ibn Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr narrated from his father that Abu Bakr al-Siddiq had divorced his wife Qutaylah in the Jahiliyyah (the period before Islam). She was the mother of Asma' bint Abi Bakr. She came to them during the period of truce between the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the disbelievers of Quraysh, and she gave gifts to Asma' bint Abi Bakr al-Siddiq, including earrings and other things. Asma' disliked accepting them until she went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and mentioned this to him. Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Allah does not forbid you from those who do not fight you over religion﴾.

al-Mawardi and others mentioned this report, and Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi recorded it in his *Musnad*.

**The second issue:** The words of Allah the Exalted ﴿that you show them kindness﴾: the word *an* (that) is in the genitive position as a substitute (*badal*) for *alladhina* (those who). The meaning is: Allah does not forbid you from showing kindness to those who do not fight you. They are Khuza'ah, who made a truce with the Prophet ﷺ that they would not fight him and would not help anyone against him. So he commanded that they be treated kindly and that the covenant with them be kept until its term. This was reported by al-Farra'.

﴿And deal justly with them﴾: this means giving them a portion of your wealth as an act of kindness. It does not mean *adl* (justice) in the sense of fairness, because justice is obligatory toward those who fight and toward those who do not fight. This was said by Ibn al-Arabi.

**The third issue:** The judge Abu Bakr said in his book *al-Ahkam*: "Some people whose fingers are pointed at (that is, notable scholars or people of reputation) used this verse as evidence that a Muslim son must support his disbelieving father." This is a serious mistake (*wahl*, a mistake made in something, as in a slip of judgment). Permission to do something, or the absence of a prohibition against it, does not prove that it is obligatory. It only shows that it is permissible. We have also explained that Isma'il ibn Ishaq the judge had a non-Muslim (*dhimmi*) visit him, and he honored him. Those present criticized him for this, so he recited this verse to them.

Allah's words: ﴿Allah only forbids you from those who fought you because of your religion﴾, meaning they waged war (jahadukum) against you over the religion, ﴿and drove you out of your homes﴾, and they were the most obstinate people of Mecca.

﴿And aided in your expulsion﴾, meaning they helped in driving you out, and they were the polytheists of the people of Mecca. ﴿That you make allies of them﴾: "an" is in the genitive position as a substitute (badal), as was explained earlier regarding "an tabarruhum."

﴿And whoever makes allies of them﴾, meaning takes them as protectors, helpers and close friends, ﴿those are the wrongdoers﴾.

**Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 60, verse 10 (part 1 of 2)**

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who believe, when believing women come to you as emigrants, then test them﴾. In it there are sixteen issues.

**The first issue:** His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who believe, when believing women come to you﴾. When He commanded the Muslims to cease allegiance (*muwalah*) to the polytheists, this required the Muslims to emigrate (*hijrah*) from the lands of polytheism to the lands of Islam. Marriage is among the most emphatic causes of allegiance, so He clarified the rulings on the emigration of women.

Ibn 'Abbas said: A truce was concluded with the polytheists of Quraysh at the year of al-Hudaybiyah, on the condition that whoever came to him (the Prophet) from the people of Makkah, he would return him to them. Then Sa'idah [[In the printed original: "Subay'ah," which is a distortion. See Usd al-Ghabah, vol. 5, p. 745.]] bint al-Harith al-Aslamiyyah came after the writing of the document was completed, while the Prophet ﷺ was still at al-Hudaybiyah. Her husband came, and he was a disbeliever, namely Safwan ibn al-Rahib. It is also said: Musafir al-Makhzumi. He said: "O Muhammad, return my wife to me, for you stipulated that! This is the clay of the document, which has not yet dried." So God, exalted is He, revealed this verse.

It is also said: Umm Kulthum bint 'Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt came, and her family came asking the Messenger of God ﷺ to return her.

It is also said: She fled from her husband 'Amr ibn al-'As, and with her were her two brothers, 'Umarah and al-Walid. The Messenger of God ﷺ returned her two brothers and detained her. They said to the Prophet ﷺ: "Return her to us according to the stipulation." He ﷺ said: "The stipulation was concerning men, not women." So God, exalted is He, revealed this verse.

From 'Urwah, who said: Among what Suhayl ibn 'Amr stipulated with the Prophet ﷺ on the day of al-Hudaybiyah was: "No one from us will come to you, even if he is upon your religion, except that you return him to us." Until God, exalted is He, revealed concerning believing women what He revealed, which points to the stipulation regarding the return of women having been abrogated by that.

It is also said that the woman who came was Umaymah bint Bishr. She had been married to Thabit ibn al-Shimrakh, and she fled from him while he was then a disbeliever. Then Sahl ibn Hunayf married her, and she bore him 'Abd Allah. This was said by Zayd ibn Habib.

Thus al-Mawardi said: Umaymah bint Bishr was married to Thabit ibn al-Shimrakh. Al-Mahdawi said: Ibn Wahb narrated from Khalid that this verse was revealed concerning Umaymah bint Bishr of the Banu 'Amr ibn 'Awf. She was the wife of Hassan ibn al-Dahdah, and after her emigration Sahl ibn Hunayf married her.

Muqatil said: She was Sa'idah [[In the printed original: "Subay'ah," which is a distortion. See Usd al-Ghabah, vol. 5, p. 745.]], the wife of Safwan ibn al-Rahib, a polytheist from the people of Makkah. The majority of the scholars hold that she was Umm Kulthum bint 'Uqbah.

**The second issue:** The scholars differed as to whether women were included in the terms of the truce (*muhadanah*), explicitly or by general application. One group said: The condition of returning them was explicitly stated in the truce agreement, so God abrogated their return from the agreement and prohibited it, and left the men under the original ruling. This indicates that the Prophet ﷺ was permitted to exercise his own judgment (*ijtihad* [[Ijtihad: exerting one's utmost effort in seeking the matter.]]) in rulings, but God does not let him persist in an error.

Another group of scholars said: The condition of returning them was not explicitly stated in the agreement. Rather, the agreement was stated in general terms concerning the return of those who embraced Islam, so the apparent generality included the women along with the men. Then God, exalted is He, clarified their exclusion from that generality. He distinguished between them and the men for two reasons: First, they are women with private parts (*furuj*) that become forbidden to the men. Second, they are more tender of heart and quicker to change than men.

As for those among them who remained upon their polytheism, they are to be returned to the polytheists.

**The third issue:** His saying, exalted is He: ﴿then test them﴾. It was said: Whenever a woman among them intended to harm her husband, she would say: "I will emigrate to Muhammad ﷺ." Therefore, the Prophet ﷺ was commanded to test them.

Scholars differed about what he would test them with, in three opinions:

The first: Ibn 'Abbas said: The test was that she be made to swear by God that she did not leave out of hatred for her husband, nor out of desire to move from land to land, nor seeking worldly gain, nor out of passion for one of our men, but rather out of love for God and His Messenger. When she swears by God, besides whom there is no god, to that, the Prophet ﷺ would give her husband his dower and what he had spent on her, and he would not return her. This is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿If you know them to be believers, then do not return them to the disbelievers; they are not lawful for them, nor are they lawful for them﴾.

The second: The test was that she bear witness that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God. Ibn 'Abbas also said this.

The third: It is what He clarified later in the surah, His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O Prophet, when believing women come to you﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 12]. 'A'ishah, may God be pleased with her, said: The Messenger of God ﷺ did not test them except with the verse which God mentioned: ﴿when believing women come to you pledging allegiance to you﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 12]. It was narrated by Ma'mar from al-Zuhri from 'A'ishah. al-Tirmidhi recorded it and said: This is a hadith that is good and sound.

**The fourth issue:** Most scholars hold that this abrogates what the Prophet ﷺ had covenanted with Quraysh, namely that he would return to them whoever came to him of them as a Muslim. So women were excluded from that ruling. This is the position of those who hold that the Sunnah can be abrogated by the Qur'an.

Some scholars said: The whole of it is abrogated concerning both men and women. It is not permissible for the ruler (*imam*) to make a truce with the enemy on the condition that he return to them whoever comes to him as a Muslim, because the residence of a Muslim in the land of polytheism is not permissible. This is the position of the Kufans. The conclusion of a truce on that basis is permissible according to Malik.

The Kufans argued for what they held in this regard with the hadith of Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid from Qays ibn Abi Hazim from Khalid ibn al-Walid, that the Messenger of God ﷺ sent him to a people from Khath'am, and they sought refuge in prostration, so he killed them. The Messenger of God ﷺ paid their blood money as half the diya, and said: "I am innocent of every Muslim who resides with a polytheist in the land of war, whose fires do not see each other."

They said: This is therefore abrogating the return of Muslims to the polytheists, since the Messenger of God ﷺ disavowed himself of whoever resided with them in the land of war.

The position of Malik and al-Shafi'i is that this ruling is not abrogated. Al-Shafi'i said: No one may conclude this agreement except the caliph or a man whom he appoints, because he is in charge of all the wealth. Whoever concludes this agreement other than the caliph, it is rejected.

**The fifth issue:** His saying, exalted is He: ﴿God knows best their faith﴾, meaning: this testing is for you, and God knows best their faith, for He is the one who takes charge of hidden matters.

﴿If you know them to be believers﴾: that is, by what appears of faith. It was said: If you know them to be believers before the testing, ﴿then do not return them to the disbelievers; they are not lawful for them, nor are they lawful for them﴾: that is, God did not make a believing woman lawful to a disbeliever, nor the marriage of a believer to a polytheist lawful.

This is the clearest proof that what dissolves the marriage of a Muslim woman from her husband is her conversion to Islam, not her emigration. Abu Hanifah said: What separates them is the difference of the two abodes (*dar*). This is alluded to in the school of Malik, indeed it is an expression. The correct position is the first, because God, exalted is He, said: ﴿they are not lawful for them, nor are they lawful for them﴾, so He made clear that the cause is the lack of lawfulness due to Islam, not the difference of abode. And God knows best.

Abu 'Umar said: There is no distinction between the two abodes, neither in the Book, nor in the Sunnah, nor in analogical reasoning. What is taken into account in this matter is the two religions. By their difference the ruling takes effect, and by their unity, not by the abode. And God is the one sought for help.

**The sixth issue:** His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and give them what they have spent﴾. God, exalted is He, commanded that when a Muslim woman is retained, what her husband had spent be returned to him. This is part of fulfilling the covenant, because when he was prevented from his wife by the sanctity of Islam, he was commanded to have the wealth returned to him, so that they do not suffer loss in two respects: the wife and the wealth.

**The seventh issue:** There is no payment (*gharm*) except when the disbelieving husband makes a claim. When he is present and makes a claim, we prevent her (from him) and we pay him. If she died before the husband's arrival, we do not pay the dower, since the prevention was not realized. If the stipulated dower was wine or pork, we pay nothing, because it has no value.

Al-Shafi'i has two opinions regarding this verse. The first: that this ruling is abrogated. Al-Shafi'i said: When a free woman from the people of the truce comes to us as a Muslim, emigrating from the land of war to the imam in the land of peace or in the land of war, whoever seeks her from a guardian other than her husband is prevented from her without compensation. If her husband seeks her for himself or for another by his agency, then there are two opinions: The first: he is given the compensation, and the saying is what God, mighty and majestic, said. The second opinion: the disbelieving husband whose wife came as a Muslim is not given compensation. If the imam stipulated the return of women, the condition is valid, and the Messenger of God ﷺ stipulated that women not be returned; so the stipulation of whoever stipulated the return of women is abrogated, and there is no compensation for it, because the abrogated stipulation is void, and there is no compensation for what is void.

[[What is between the brackets is thus found in all the manuscripts of the original, and it is confused. The author, may God have mercy on him, transmitted this issue from the book al-Nasikh wa'l-Mansukh by Abu Ja'far al-Nahhas, and its text there is: "If the imam stipulates the return of women, the condition is invalidated. Whoever says this says: If the Messenger of God ﷺ stipulated for the people of al-Hudaybiyah that whoever came from them would be returned, and women were among them, it was a valid condition. Then God abrogated it and the compensation was returned. **The eighth issue:** Allah, exalted is He, commanded that the equivalent of what they (the husbands) had spent be returned to the (believing) wives. The one addressed by this is the ruler (*imam*), who disburses from what is in his hands of the public treasury (*bayt al-mal*), which has no specific designated use. Muqatil said: he returns the dowry, and whoever marries her from among the Muslims pays it; if none of the Muslims marries her, then her disbelieving husband has no claim. Qatadah said: the ruling on returning the dowry applies only to the women of the people of covenant (*ahl al-'ahd*). As for one who has no covenant between himself and the Muslims, the dowry is not returned to them. The matter is as he said [[In ḥ, z, s: "as he said, may Allah have mercy on him."]].

**The ninth issue:** His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And there is no blame upon you in marrying them﴾, meaning once they have embraced Islam and their waiting period (*'iddah*) has ended, because of the established prohibition of marrying a polytheist woman and a woman in her waiting period. If she embraces Islam before consummation, the marriage is established immediately, and she may remarry.

**The tenth issue:** His saying, exalted is He: ﴿When you have given them their compensation﴾ permits marrying them on condition of the dowry, because Islam has separated her from her disbelieving husband [[In s: "on condition of Islam, because the dowry and Islam..."]].

**The eleventh issue:** His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not hold on to the disbelieving women by marriage ties﴾. The reading of the majority is with the light form (*takhfif*) from *al-imsak* (holding). This is the choice of Abu 'Ubayd, due to His saying, exalted is He: "then retain them honourably" (Al-Baqarah 2:231). Al-Hasan, Abu al-'Aliyah and Abu 'Amr read *wa-la tumassikū* with a doubled *sīn* from *al-tamassuk*. It is said: *massaka yumassiku tamassuka*, with the same meaning as *amsaka yumsiku*. It has also been read *wa-la tamsikū* with a fatha on the *tā'*, meaning: do not cling to. *Al-'iṣam* is the plural of *al-'iṣmah*, which is that by which one holds fast. The intended meaning of *al-'iṣmah* here is the marriage bond. The meaning is: whoever has a disbelieving wife in Makkah, let him not consider her as his, for she is no longer his wife, since her bond has been severed by the difference of the two abodes. It is related from al-Nakha'i: it refers to a Muslim woman who joins the abode of war and then disbelieves. The disbelievers used to marry Muslim women and the Muslims used to marry polytheist women, and then this was abrogated (*nusikha*) by this verse. Accordingly, 'Umar ibn al-Khattab divorced at that time two of his wives in Makkah who were polytheists: Qurayba bint Abi Umayyah, who was then married to Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan while both were still upon their polytheism in Makkah; and Umm Kulthum bint 'Amr al-Khuza'iyyah, mother of 'Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, who was then married to Abu Jahm ibn Hudhayfah while both were upon their polytheism. When 'Umar became caliph, Abu Sufyan said to Mu'awiyah: "Divorce Qurayba, so that 'Umar does not see his spoils in your house." Mu'awiyah refused to do so. Arwa bint Rabi'ah ibn al-Harith ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib was married to Talhah ibn 'Ubaydullah, and Islam separated them. Then she was married, in Islam, to Khalid ibn Sa'id ibn al-'As. She was among the disbelieving women who fled to the Prophet ﷺ, and he kept her and married her to Khalid. The Prophet ﷺ also married his daughter Zaynab, who was then a disbeliever, to Abu al-'As ibn al-Rabi'; then she embraced Islam and her husband embraced Islam after her.

'Abd al-Razzaq related, from Ibn Jurayj, from a man, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Zaynab, the daughter of the Prophet ﷺ, embraced Islam and emigrated after the Prophet ﷺ, in the first emigration, while her husband Abu al-'As ibn al-Rabi', 'Abd al-'Uzza, was a polytheist in Makkah. The hadith [continues], and in it: he embraced Islam after her. Al-Sha'bi also said likewise. Al-Sha'bi said: Zaynab, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, was the wife of Abu al-'As ibn al-Rabi'. She embraced Islam and then joined the Prophet ﷺ. Then her husband came to Madinah, she granted him protection, he embraced Islam, and the Prophet ﷺ returned her to him.

Abu Dawud related from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: "with the first marriage contract, and he did not introduce anything new." Muhammad ibn 'Umar said in his narration: after six years. Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali said: after two years. Abu 'Umar [Ibn 'Abd al-Barr] said: If this is authentic, then it has one of two possibilities: either she had not menstruated until her husband embraced Islam, or the ruling in it has been abrogated by the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "and their husbands have more right to take them back in that [period]" (Al-Baqarah 2:228), meaning within their waiting period. There is no disagreement among the scholars that this refers to the waiting period. Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri, may Allah have mercy on him, said regarding the story of Zaynab: this was before the obligatory shares (*al-fara'id*) were revealed. Qatadah said: this was before the Surah "Bara'ah" was revealed, which cut the covenants between them and the polytheists. And Allah knows best.

**The twelfth issue:** His saying, exalted is He: ﴿by the marriage ties of the disbelieving women﴾. The intended meaning of *al-kawāfir* here is the idol-worshippers, whom it is not permissible to marry initially. So it is specific to disbelieving women other than the People of the Book. It has been said: it is general, and the women of the People of the Book were abrogated from it. Had it remained according to the apparent meaning of the verse, no disbelieving woman would ever be lawful. According to the first view, if a idol-worshipper or Magian (*majusi*) embraces Islam and his wife does not embrace Islam, they are separated. This is the view of some scholars. Others said: he waits for her to complete the waiting period. Whoever says they are separated immediately, without waiting for the completion of the waiting period, when Islam is presented to her and she does not embrace it, is Malik ibn Anas. This is also the view of al-Hasan, Tawus, Mujahid, 'Ata', 'Ikrimah, Qatadah and al-Hakam, and they argued with His saying, exalted is He: "And do not hold on to the disbelieving women by marriage ties." Al-Zuhri said: he waits for her to complete the waiting period. This is the view of al-Shafi'i and Ahmad. They argued that Abu Sufyan ibn Harb embraced Islam before his wife Hind bint 'Utbah, and his embracing Islam was at Marr al-Zahran [[Marr al-Zahran: a village near Makkah.]]. Then he returned to Makkah while Hind was there, a disbeliever remaining upon her disbelief. She took hold of his beard and said: "Kill this misguided old man!" Then she embraced Islam a few days after him, and they remained upon their marriage, because her waiting period had not ended. They said: Similarly, Hakim ibn Hizam embraced Islam before his wife, and then she embraced Islam after him, and they remained upon their marriage. Al-Shafi'i said: There is no proof for those who argue with His saying, exalted is He: "And do not hold on to the disbelieving women by marriage ties," because Muslim women are forbidden to disbelievers, just as Muslims may not lawfully marry disbelieving women, idolatresses or Magian women, by the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "They are not lawful for them, nor are they lawful for them." Then the Sunnah clarified that the intended meaning of His saying is that some of them are not lawful for others unless the remaining one of the two embraces Islam within the waiting period.

As for the Kufans, namely Sufyan and Abu Hanifah and his companions, they said regarding protected non-Muslim subjects (*dhimmis*): when the woman embraces Islam, Islam is presented to the husband; if he embraces it, well and good, and otherwise they are separated. They said: If both were in the abode of war, she remains his wife until she menstruates three times, whether both are in the abode of war or both are in the abode of Islam. If one of them is in the abode of Islam and the other in the abode of war, the bond between them is severed, so they consider the abode. But this is nothing, and it has already been mentioned.

**The thirteenth issue:** This disagreement applies only to a woman with whom the marriage has been consummated. If she was not consummated, we know of no disagreement that the bond between them is severed, since she has no waiting period. Thus Malik says regarding a woman whose husband apostatised (*irtidad*): the bond between them is severed. His proof is: "And do not hold on to the disbelieving women by marriage ties." This is the view of al-Hasan al-Basri and al-Hasan ibn Salih ibn Hayy. The position of al-Shafi'i and Ahmad is that he waits for her to complete the waiting period.

**The fourteenth issue:** If the spouses are both Christians and the wife embraces Islam, there is also a disagreement on this. The position of Malik, Ahmad and al-Shafi'i is to wait until the waiting period is completed. This is also the view of Mujahid. Likewise, if a polytheist's wife embraces Islam: if he embraces Islam during her waiting period, he has more right to her, just as Safwan ibn Umayyah and 'Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl had more right to their two wives when they embraced Islam during their waiting periods, according to the hadith of Ibn Shihab. Malik related it in the *Muwatta'*. Ibn Shihab said: the interval between Safwan's embracing Islam and his wife's embracing Islam was about a month. Ibn Shihab also said: It has not reached us that a woman emigrated to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while her husband, a disbeliever, remained in the abode of war, except that her emigration separated her from him, unless her husband came as an emigrant before her waiting period ended. Some scholars said: the marriage is annulled between them. Yazid ibn 'Alqamah said: My grandfather embraced Islam and my grandmother did not embrace Islam, so 'Umar separated them, may Allah be pleased with him. This is also the view of Tawus. A group besides him, including 'Ata', al-Hasan and 'Ikrimah, said: there is no way (for him) over her except by a new marriage proposal (*khutbah*).

**The fifteenth issue:** His saying, exalted is He: (﴿And ask for what you spent, and let them ask for what they spent﴾). The commentators (*al-mufassirun*) said: whoever of the Muslim women went over to the disbelievers from among the people of covenant, it was said to the disbelievers: "Hand over her dowry." And it was said to the Muslims, when one of the disbelieving women came to them as a Muslim emigrant: "Return her dowry to the disbelievers." That was a just and equitable arrangement between the two situations. This was the ruling of Allah, specific to that time and to that particular case, by the consensus (*ijma'*) of the community, said Ibn al-'Arabi.

**The sixteenth issue:** His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That is the judgement of Allah﴾, meaning what has been mentioned in this verse, (﴿He judges between you, and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾). It has been discussed previously in more than one place [[See vol. 1, p. 287.]].

**Issue one:** Concerning the words of the Most High, ﴿And if any of your wives have gone over to the disbelievers, and you then have a victory, give to those whose wives have gone the equivalent of what they had spent.﴾ It is reported that the Muslims said, "We are content with what Allah has decreed," and they wrote to the polytheists, but the polytheists refused. Then this was revealed: ﴿And if any of your wives have gone over to the disbelievers, and you then have a victory...﴾ ﴿...give to those whose wives have gone the equivalent of what they had spent.﴾

Al-Zuhri narrated from Urwa, from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, judged between you, and He said, ﴿And ask for what you have spent, and let them ask for what they have spent.﴾ So the Muslims wrote to them: 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has judged between us that if a woman from us comes to you, you must send her dowry to us, and if a woman from you comes to us, we will send her dowry to you.' They wrote back to them: 'As for us, we do not know of anything owed to you. But if we are owed anything by you, then send it to us.' So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And if any of your wives have gone over to the disbelievers, and you then have a victory, give to those whose wives have gone the equivalent of what they had spent.﴾"

Ibn Abbas said concerning the words of the Most High, ﴿That is the judgement of Allah; He judges between you﴾: that is, between the Muslims and the disbelievers of the covenant from the people of Makkah, some of whom return to others. Al-Zuhri said: "Had there been no covenant, he would have kept the women and not returned their dowries to them."

Qatada and Mujahid said: "They were only ordered to give those whose wives had gone the equivalent of what they had spent from the fay' (spoils taken without battle) and the ghanima (war booty)." And they said: "It applies to those between us and whom there is a covenant, and not to those between us and whom there is no covenant."

They also said: "The meaning of ﴿you then have a victory﴾ is ﴿you then take retribution.﴾ ﴿Give to those whose wives have gone the equivalent of what they had spent﴾ means the dowries." Thus it is general, covering all disbelievers.

Qatada also said: "And if any of your wives have gone over to the disbelievers" – those disbelievers ﴿with whom you have a covenant﴾ – ﴿give to those whose wives have gone the equivalent of what they had spent.﴾ Then this was abrogated (naskh) in Surat Bara'a (At-Tawba). Al-Zuhri said: "This ended in the year of the conquest (of Makkah)." Sufyan al-Thawri said: "It is not acted upon today." Others said: "Its ruling is still firmly established even now." This was related by al-Qushayri.

**Issue two:** Concerning the words of the Most High, ﴿you then have a victory﴾. The reading of the majority is فَعَاقَبْتُمْ (fa-'aqabtum). Alqama, al-Nakha'i, Humayd and al-A'raj read فَعَقَّبْتُمْ (fa-'aqqabtum) with a shadda. Mujahid read فَأَعْقَبْتُمْ (fa-a'qabtum) and said: "You did as they had done to you." Al-Zuhri read فَعَقَبْتُمْ (fa-'aqabtum) without the alif and without the shadda. Masruq and Shaqiq ibn Salama read فَعَقِبْتُمْ (fa-'aqibtum) with a kasra on the qaf and without the shadda, and said: "You gained booty." All of these are dialectal variants with the same meaning. It is said: 'aqaba, 'aqaba, 'aqqaba, a'qaba, ta'aqqaba, i'taqaba and ta'aqaba, meaning "he gained booty." Al-Qutabi said: "fa-'aqabtum means you went out to war, one after another, in a series of raids." Ibn Bahr said: "That is, if you retaliated against the apostate woman by killing her, then her husband is owed her dowry from the booty of the Muslims."

**Issue three:** Concerning the words of the Most High, ﴿give to those whose wives have gone the equivalent of what they had spent﴾. Ibn Abbas said: "The meaning is: if a believing woman joins the disbelievers of the people of Makkah, and there is no covenant between you and them, and she has a Muslim husband among you, and you take booty, then give this Muslim husband his dowry from the booty before it is divided into fifths (khums)."

Al-Zuhri said: "He is given from the fay' property." He also said: "He is given from the dowry of the one who joined us." It was also said: "That is, if they refuse to pay the dowry of this woman who went to them, then cast the covenant back to them, so that when you gain victory you may take that from them."

Al-A'mash said: "It has been abrogated." Ata' said: "Rather, its ruling is still established." All of this has been mentioned previously.

Al-Qushayri said: "The verse was revealed concerning Umm al-Hakam bint Abi Sufyan, who apostatized and left her husband Iyad ibn Ghanm al-Qurashi. No woman of Quraysh apostatized other than her, and then she returned to Islam."

Al-Tha'labi related from Ibn Abbas: "They were six women who turned away from Islam and joined the polytheists from among the wives of the emigrant believers: Umm al-Hakam bint Abi Sufyan, who was married to Iyad ibn Abi Shaddad al-Fihri;[[He is Iyad ibn Ghanm ibn Zuhayr ibn Abi Shaddad al-Qurashi al-Fihri.]] Fatima bint Abi Umayya ibn al-Mughira, sister of Umm Salama, who was married to Umar ibn al-Khattab, and when Umar emigrated she refused and apostatized; Barwa' bint Uqba, who was married to Shammas ibn Uthman; Abda bint Abd al-Uzza, who was married to Hisham ibn al-As; Umm Kulthum bint Jarwal, who was married to Umar ibn al-Khattab; and Shihba bint Ghaylan." So the Prophet (ﷺ) gave their husbands the dowries of their wives from the booty.

(And fear Allah) – beware lest you transgress what you have been commanded.

**Issue one (part 1 of 2):** ﴿O Prophet, when believing women come to you pledging allegiance to you...﴾ [[What is between the two brackets is omitted from MS L and MS Z.]] When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) conquered Makkah, the women of Makkah came to him to pledge allegiance, so he was commanded to take from them the pledge that they would not associate anything with Allah. In the Sahih of Muslim, on the authority of Aishah, the wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), she said: "When believing women emigrated to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), they were tested (*imtihan*, the test) by the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿O Prophet, when believing women come to you pledging allegiance to you, that they will not associate anything with Allah, nor steal, nor commit adultery...﴾ to the end of the verse." Aishah said: "Whoever of the believing women affirmed this had affirmed the test. When they affirmed this in their words, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would say to them: 'Go, for I have pledged allegiance to you.' By Allah, the hand of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) never touched the hand of a woman; he pledged allegiance to them only by speech." Aishah also said: "By Allah, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) never took anything from the women except what Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, had commanded him, and the palm of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) never touched the palm of a woman. He would say to them when he had taken their pledge: 'I have pledged allegiance to you by word.'"

It is also narrated that the peace and blessings of Allah be upon him pledged allegiance to the women while a cloth was between his hand and their hands, and that he would stipulate conditions upon them. It was said: When he had finished the pledge of the men, he sat upon al-Safa, with Umar beneath him, and he began to stipulate the pledge upon the women while Umar shook hands with them. It is also narrated that he assigned a woman who stood upon al-Safa to pledge allegiance to them. Ibn al-Arabi said: "That is weak; reliance should be placed only on what is in the Sahih."

Umm Atiyyah said: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) arrived in Madinah, he gathered the women of the Ansar in one house, then sent Umar ibn al-Khattab to us. He stood at the door and greeted us with salam, and we returned his greeting. He said: 'I am the messenger of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to you, that you not associate anything with Allah.' We said: 'Yes.' He extended his hand from outside the house and we extended our hands from inside the house. Then he said: 'O Allah, bear witness.'"

Amr ibn Shu'ayb narrated from his father, from his grandfather, that the Prophet (ﷺ), whenever he pledged allegiance to women, would call for a vessel of water, dip his hand into it, and then command the women to dip their hands into it.

**Issue two:** It is narrated that when the Prophet (ﷺ) said: ﴿that they will not associate anything with Allah﴾, Hind bint Utbah, while veiled out of fear that the Prophet (ﷺ) would recognise her because of what she had done to Hamzah on the day of Uhud, said: "By Allah, you are taking from us a matter which I have not seen you take from men," for he had pledged the men that day only to Islam and jihad. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "and that they will not steal." Hind said: "Abu Sufyan is a stingy man, and I take from his wealth to feed us." Abu Sufyan said: "It is lawful for you." The Prophet (ﷺ) laughed, recognised her, and said: "Are you Hind?" She said: "Allah has pardoned what has passed." Then he said: "and that they will not commit adultery." Hind said: "Does a free woman commit adultery?" Then he said: "and that they will not kill their children," meaning they should not bury alive their infant daughters nor abort their fetuses. Hind said: "We raised them as small children, and you killed them as grown men on the day of Badr, so you and they know best." It is narrated by Muqatil that she said: "We raised them as little ones, and you killed them as grown men, and you and they know best." Umar ibn al-Khattab laughed until he lay on his back. Hanzalah ibn Abi Sufyan, who was her virgin child, had been killed on the day of Badr.

Then he said: ﴿nor bring a slander they have invented between their hands and their feet﴾, and ﴿nor disobey you in what is right﴾. It was said: The meaning of "between their hands" is their tongues, through backbiting (*namimah*), and the meaning of "between their feet" is their private parts. It was also said: what is between their hands is kissing or touching, and what is between their feet is intercourse. It was also said: the meaning is that they should not attribute to their husbands a child that is not theirs; this is the view of the majority. A woman would pick up a child and attribute it to her husband, saying: "This is my child from you," and this was counted as slander and fabrication. It was also said: "what is between her hands and her feet" is a metaphor for the child, because the belly in which she carries the child is between her hands, and her womb from which she gives birth is between her feet. This is general in bringing a child and attributing it to the husband, even though the prohibition of fornication had already preceded it.

It is narrated that when Hind heard this, she said: "By Allah, slander is a shameful matter; he commands only what is most right and noble of character!"

Then he said: ﴿nor disobey you in what is right﴾. Qatadah said: "That is, that they should not wail." And that no woman among them should be alone except with a mahram. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Muhammad ibn al-Sa'ib and Zayd ibn Aslam said: It means that they should not scratch the face, nor tear the collar, nor call out woe, nor loosen the hair, nor speak to men except with a mahram. Umm Atiyyah narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that this refers to wailing, and this is the view of Ibn Abbas. Shahr ibn Hawshab narrated from Umm Salamah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding ﴿nor disobey you in what is right﴾, and he said: "It is wailing." Musab ibn Nuh said: "I met an old woman from among those who pledged allegiance to the Prophet (ﷺ), and she related to me from him, peace and blessings be upon him, regarding the saying ﴿nor disobey you in what is right﴾, that he said: 'It is wailing.'"

In the Sahih of Muslim, on the authority of Umm Atiyyah: when this verse was revealed, ﴿they will not associate anything with Allah﴾ up to ﴿nor disobey you in what is right﴾, he said: "Among it is wailing." She said: "I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, except the family of so-and-so, for they used to help me in the Jahiliyyah, so I must help them.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Except the family of so-and-so.'" And from her: she said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took from us, along with the pledge, that we would not wail. None of us fulfilled it except five women: Umm Sulaym, Umm al-Ala, the daughter of Abu Sabrah, the wife of Mu'adh (or the daughter of Abu Sabrah and the wife of Mu'adh), and the wife of Mu'adh."

It was said: The meaning of "what is right" here is obedience to Allah and His Messenger, as said by Maymun ibn Mihran. Bakr ibn Abdullah al-Muzani said: ﴿nor disobey you in what is right﴾ means in every matter in which there is their guidance. Al-Kalbi said: It is general for every right thing that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and His Messenger commanded. It is narrated that Hind then said: "We did not sit in this gathering of ours while we had in our hearts that we would disobey you in anything."

**Issue three:** Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and His Messenger (ﷺ) mentioned in the description of the pledge various characteristics, in which he explicitly stated the pillars of prohibition in the religion but did not mention the pillars of command. These are also six: the testimony of faith, prayer, zakat, fasting, hajj, and the ghusl from major impurity. This is because prohibition is constant in all times and all states, so drawing attention to the stipulation of what is constant is more emphatic. It was also said: among women there were many who committed these prohibited acts and whom the nobility of their lineage did not restrain, so they were singled out for mention because of this. Similar to this is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) to the delegation of Abd al-Qays: "I forbid you from the gourd (*dubba'*), the jar (*hantam*), the palm-trunk vessel (*naqir*), and the coated vessel (*muzaffat*)." [[Al-Dubba': the dried gourd. Al-Hantam: a jar. Al-Naqir: the base of a palm tree, hollowed out and made into a container. Al-Muzaffat: a vessel coated with pitch. Al-Zurqani said in his commentary on al-Mawahib al-Ladunniyyah: "On the authority of Abu Bakrah, he said: As for the gourd, the people of al-Ta'if would take gourds, hollow them out, put grapes in them, and bury them until they ferment and then die. As for the palm-trunk vessel, the people of al-Yamamah would hollow out the base of a palm tree, then steep fresh dates and unripe dates in it, and leave it until it ferments and dies. As for the jar, they were jars in which wine was brought to us. As for the coated vessel, these are the containers coated with pitch... The prohibition of steeping in these particular vessels is because intoxication comes quickly to them, so someone may drink from them without realising it. Then permission was established for steeping in every vessel, with the prohibition on drinking any intoxicant."]] So he drew their attention to abstaining from the disobedience of drinking wine, rather than the other sins, because it was their desire and habit; and when a person gives up his desire among the sins, it becomes easy for him to abandon the rest of those for which he has no desire.

The Fourth: When the Prophet ﷺ said in the pledge, "and they shall not steal," Hind said, "O Messenger of Allah, Abu Sufyan is a stingy man. Is there any blame on me if I take what suffices me and my child?" He said, "No, except in what is customary (bi-l-ma'ruf)." Hind feared that she would be limited to what he gave her and would be ruined, or that she would take more than that and thereby become a thief who breaks the pledge mentioned. The Prophet ﷺ said to her, "No. There is no blame on you for what you have taken in accordance with what is customary," meaning without excess beyond the need. Ibn al-Arabi said: This applies only to what he does not keep from her in his private store and does not secure with a lock. If the wife breaks into that and takes from it, she is a thief who disobeys by doing so, and her hand is cut off.

The Fifth: Ubada ibn al-Samit said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took the pledge from us as he took it from the women: "That you will not associate anything with Allah, nor steal, nor commit adultery, nor kill your children, nor slander (ya'dah) one another, nor disobey in what is customary that He commands you." The meaning of "ya'dah" is "to practise sorcery," and al-'Adhah is sorcery. For this reason Ibn Bahr and others said, regarding the words of the Exalted, ﴿nor bring a false charge (bi-buhtan)﴾, that it is sorcery. Al-Dahhak said: This is a prohibition against false accusation (buhtan), meaning that they should not accuse a man or a woman of buhtan, that is, of sorcery. And Allah knows best. ﴿Which they forge between their hands and their feet﴾. The majority hold that the meaning of "with a false charge" concerning a child which they fabricate "between their hands and their feet" is: "what she has taken as a foundling (laqit)," and "their feet" means what she has borne from fornication. This has already been discussed.

The Sixth: His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿nor disobey you in what is customary﴾. Al-Bukhari reported from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying, ﴿nor disobey you in what is customary﴾, that he said: "It is only a condition which Allah imposed upon the women." Its meaning has been differed over, as we have mentioned. The sound view is that it is general to everything that the Prophet ﷺ commands and forbids. It includes wailing (niyaha), tearing garments, shaving the hair, seclusion with a non-mahram, and other things. All of these are major sins (kaba'ir) and among the practices of the Jahiliyyah. In Sahih Muslim, from Abu Malik al-Ash'ari, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Four matters of the Jahiliyyah remain among my community," and he mentioned among them wailing. Yahya ibn Abi Kathir related from Abu Salama, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "These wailing women will be brought on the Day of Resurrection in two rows: a row on the right and a row on the left, barking like dogs, on a day whose measure is fifty thousand years. Then they will be commanded to the Fire." And from him (Abu Hurayra) who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The angels do not send blessings upon a wailing woman or a woman who wails loudly [[al-irnan: a severe cry and a sorrowful voice during singing or weeping; it is said: rannat al-mar'ah tarunnu rununan, and arnat, meaning she cried out.]]." It is related from Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, that he heard a wailing woman, went to her, and struck her with a whip until her head covering fell from her head. It was said to him: "O Commander of the Faithful, the woman, the woman! Her head covering has fallen." He said: "She has no sanctity." Al-Tha'labi, may Allah have mercy on him, traced all of this with its chains of narration.

As for specifying His saying, "in what is customary," alongside the strength of His saying, ﴿nor disobey you﴾, there are two views. The first: it is an explanation of the meaning for emphasis, as He said, ﴿He said: My Lord, judge with truth﴾ [[See vol. 11, p. (350).]] [al-Anbiya': 112], because if He had said "judge," it would have been sufficient. The second: the condition of "what is customary" was made in the pledge to the Prophet ﷺ so as to alert that others are more entitled to it, more bound by it, and that it removes ambiguity.

The Seventh: Al-Bukhari reported from Ubada ibn al-Samit, who said: We were with the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: "Will you pledge allegiance to me that you will not associate anything with Allah, nor commit adultery, nor steal?" and he recited the verse of the women. The wording of Sufyan is mostly: he recited in the verse, "So whoever of you fulfils it, his reward is with Allah; and whoever commits any of that and is punished for it, that is an expiation for him; and whoever commits any of that and Allah conceals it, then it is up to Allah: if He wills, He punishes him, and if He wills, He forgives him for it." In the Two Sahihs, from Ibn Abbas, who said: I witnessed the prayer of the day of Fitr with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman. All of them would pray it before the sermon, then deliver the sermon. The Prophet of Allah ﷺ then descended, and it is as if I am looking at him when he seats the men with his hand. Then he came forward, pushing through them until he reached the women with Bilal, and said: "O Prophet, when the believing women come to you pledging allegiance to you that they will not associate anything with Allah, nor steal, nor commit adultery, nor kill their children, nor bring a false charge which they forge between their hands and their feet," until he finished the whole verse. Then, when he finished, he said: "Do you agree to this?" One woman, and no one else answered him, said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." Al-Hasan [[This is al-Hasan ibn Muslim, the narrator of the hadith.]] did not know who she was. He said: "Then give charity." Bilal spread out his garment, and they began to throw down the rings (fatakh) and the finger rings into Bilal's garment. This is the wording of al-Bukhari.

The Eighth: Al-Mahdawi said: The Muslims are agreed that it is not for the imam to impose this condition upon them, and the command to it is recommendation (nadb), not obligation. Some scholars of reasoning (ahl al-nazar) said: If a test (mihna) is needed because of the distance of the abode, it is incumbent upon the imam of the Muslims to establish the test.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 60, verse 13:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take as allies a people with whom Allah is angry﴾, meaning the Jews. The reason is that some of the poor Muslims used to inform the Jews of the news of the believers and maintain ties with them, and thereby they would obtain some of their fruits, so they were forbidden from doing so.

(﴿They have despaired of the Hereafter﴾), meaning the Jews, as said by Ibn Zayd. It was also said: they are the hypocrites. al-Hasan said: they are the Jews and the Christians. Ibn Mas'ud said: its meaning is that they abandoned work for the Hereafter and preferred this world. It was also said: the meaning is that they despaired of the reward of the Hereafter, as said by Mujahid. And the meaning of (﴿as the disbelievers have despaired﴾) is: the living among the disbelievers.

(﴿of those in the graves﴾), that they would return to them, as said by al-Hasan and Qatadah. Ibn 'Arafah said: they are those who said: ﴿And nothing destroys us except time﴾ [al-Jathiyah 24]. Mujahid said: the meaning is, as the disbelievers who are in the graves have despaired of returning to the world. It was also said: Allah, exalted is He, concluded the surah with what He began it with, namely the prohibition of allying with the disbelievers, and it is addressed to Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah and others. Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take as allies﴾, i.e., do not befriend them and do not advise them. Allah, exalted is He, in His bounty and grace, relented toward Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah. He means that the disbelievers of Quraysh have despaired of the good of the Hereafter, as the disbelievers in the graves have despaired of any share they would have in the Hereafter from the mercy of Allah, exalted is He. al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah, regarding His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿they have despaired of the Hereafter, as the disbelievers have despaired of those in the graves﴾, said: whoever of the disbelievers dies has despaired of good. And Allah knows best.
